parts.t: Aberdeen is in the southwest corner of Abbotsford, next to the Langley border. It is mostly farmland and includes the Pepin Brook community, Aldergrove Regional Park and the Fraser Highway. The area takes its name from Aberdeen school, named after its Scottish settlers.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 12, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate for 11+ years. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Abbotsford and the Agricultural Land Commission.
None of this is legal, planning or financial advice. Ahead of any purchase or sale in Aberdeen, look up the zoning and the community plan, and find out which schools cover the address.

blocks.text: Planning and the ALR in Aberdeen

parts.t: Aberdeen doesn’t have a neighbourhood plan of its own. Instead, the ALR rules and the City’s Official Community Plan (OCP) govern each property separately.

For a home that runs on a well, have the flow tested along with the water quality, and ask whether earlier test results are available.
Find out how old the system is and when it was last serviced, and have it inspected.

Find out whether other parties hold rights or restrictions on the land, such as covenants, rights of way and easements, and that includes any access you depend on.
Setback rules for streams can restrict where on the lot you can build. Ask the City of Abbotsford whether a watercourse crosses or sits next to the land.
